CORRECTED 2026-10-11 FROM THE LEAD'S FIELD EVIDENCE - THE STOP WORKS; THE BADGE DOES NOT CLEAR, and that is the defect. First filed as "the Stop does not stop it", which was WRONG about its central fact. The state, read from GET /api/screen after the fact: state "ended", on false, paused null, left_s null, ended "owner", ended_words "you stopped it" - the backend had ALREADY ended the session before the read. The badge window was still on screen ten minutes later saying "Jarvis is watching - paused" and "Paused: one of Jarvis's own windows - 8 min left", its Stop still offering to stop nothing, while the number it showed counted down on its own. THE HARM IS THE SIGN ITSELF: a stale "Jarvis is watching" badge is a FALSE PRIVACY ALARM, in the one feature whose whole promise is a visible sign plus an instant stop, and the owner will act on it. CAUSE, TRACED - the badge is EVENT-ONLY after startup and never re-reads: watch-badge.js:156 listens for the screen-status event, :161 reads screen_status ONCE at startup, and render() re-schedules itself every 10 s while sign.on and current() decrements left_s LOCALLY from the last payload - which is exactly why a frozen payload looks alive, with a decreasing countdown. The desktop emits screen-status only when THE APP ITSELF makes the call (look.rs:551-552 run_watch -> on_status -> :468 emit_all), and on_status hides the badge only in its else-if-was branch after BADGE_ENDED_FOR, 15 s (look.rs:476-485). So ANY ending that does not come through this app's own screen_watch command - another client, the voice or quick "stop watching" path (screen_stop), the countdown running out on the PC, a watchdog - leaves the badge up for ever. Two readings of this field case remain, and each is testable: either the ending came from a path that emits nothing, or it came from the app and the event never reached the badge window's listener. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ALREADY ON THE SCREEN: the bar and the tray follow the SAME on_status, so if the Jarvis bar still shows a watching sign, the app never learned; if the bar cleared and only the badge is stale, the event reached the app but not the badge window. Also noted: ended "owner" is the string ENGINE.stop() writes (jarvis_screen.py:1312-1314), so the ending was a POST /api/screen stop and not the hotkey, whose stop_everything() writes "stop_all" (:1649). ALREADY REFUTED, kept for the record: the paused state is not the cause (jarvis_screen.py:1310 and :1646 both end a PAUSED session) and the verb is accepted from anywhere (ANY_DOS :1814). NOT CHANGED AND NOT TO BE CHANGED: the pause rule and the sign's wording behaved correctly. WHAT A FIX MUST DO, and it is not done here: the badge must be able to learn the session ended WITHOUT this app being the one that ended it - a status re-read on the same 10 s tick it already runs, with the existing 15 s ended display then closing it. The live backend and the running prebuilt app were not reachable from the investigating branch. LIVE REPRODUCTION ADDED 2026-10-11, BOTH READ IN THE SAME MINUTE: the badge on screen said "Jarvis is watching - paused" and "Paused: one of Jarvis's own windows - under a minute left" while GET /api/screen in that same minute said state=ended, on=False, paused=, left_s=, ended=owner, ended_words="you stopped it". The session had been stopped at about 17 minutes left, and the sign counted all the way down to under a minute while the backend said ended the whole time. THE FIGURE THAT MATTERS, and it is arithmetic from the API rather than an estimate: the sign does not linger for BADGE_ENDED_FOR (15 s) - its own local arithmetic is the only thing driving it, so it lingers for the WHOLE REMAINING COUNTDOWN, and the largest session is 120 minutes (max_minutes in the same /api/screen answer). SO THE SIGN CAN CLAIM "JARVIS IS WATCHING" FOR UP TO TWO HOURS AFTER WATCHING STOPPED. That is why the fix's bound must be one tick plus the ended display (25 s) REGARDLESS of how much countdown was left, which is what tests/look-rules.mjs pins, and why the earlier wording "stale by a few seconds" would have understated it. AND PAST THE COUNTDOWN IT LINGERS INDEFINITELY - CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-10-11: with the backend at state=ended the minutes line bottomed out at "under a minute left" and the sign SIMPLY STAYED, still saying "Jarvis is watching - paused", and it is still on screen now. The failing build has NO close path at all: the frozen payload keeps watchOn(s) true, render() keeps re-scheduling itself every 10 s, and Rust's hide_badge only runs on the on-to-off transition that on_status itself observed. So "lingers for the remaining countdown" is TOO KIND - it does not clear late, IT DOES NOT CLEAR AT ALL, and it sits there claiming Jarvis is watching until the app is restarted. That is why the fix re-reads rather than merely re-rendering, and why its own closeBadge() matters: with it the sign is gone within one tick plus the ended display (25 s) whatever was left. THE STALE STATE IS NOT ONLY IN THE BADGE: the bar's own Watch with me control reported Off while the sign stayed up, so two of the app's own surfaces disagree with the backend AND WITH EACH OTHER - the badge is the worst one only because it is the surface a person sees. AND THE RUST HIDE IS TRANSITION-GATED AND ONE-SHOT, which is why pressing Stop again cannot clear a stray badge: look.rs:465-485 computes was = ON_HERE.swap(on, ...) and reaches hide_badge ONLY inside "else if was", then re-checks !on_here() 15 s later. Once the app's own flag has settled to false there is no transition left to observe, so no hide is scheduled at all - no retry, no idempotence, and a second Stop cannot re-trigger it. DATING THE PATH, so the running build can be judged rather than guessed: fn hide_badge and BADGE_ENDED_FOR were BOTH introduced on 2026-09-29 by 5fbf0371, the original "Watch with me" commit - so any build that has the badge at all also has this path, which dates the running app after it. The repository's version field cannot answer the question either: tauri.conf.json and Cargo.toml both still read 0.2.0, so 0.2.140 is a build number that does not come from it. CLOSED 2026-10-12: the fix is in main. #302 added the badge's re-read on the tick it already ran, the freeze on stale news, closeBadge() and the one capability line it needed, and tests/look-rules.mjs pins 'one tick plus the ended display (25 s)' and BITES (a synthetic open row... no: a mutation of the guard fails it). HONEST LIMIT: the desk-side re-drive of a REAL frozen badge never happened - the stale window carries the old script and cannot be reloaded without restarting the app, so only the test proves it, not the owner's machine.

STRUCTURAL DEFECT, not a code bug, and the fix is a SHAPE change rather than a patch. docs/README.md carries the number of documents and the total size of docs/ as HAND-TYPED values, and every docs pull request edits those same lines - so any two docs PRs conflict BY CONSTRUCTION. MEASURED 2026-10-11, and this is arithmetic rather than opinion: between two consecutive runs of tools/check_docs_map.py on ONE tree, the byte figure moved 8,417,863 -> 8,417,870, because WRITING THE FIGURE INTO THE PAGE CHANGED THE PAGE. A hand-typed value that changes when you write it is a value no pull request can ever get right and leave alone. THE COST, counted from tonight alone: the page or the register beside it was touched or re-synced by #291, #296, #302, #310, #312, #320 and #325; three of the day's conflicts were this page alone (#310's and #304's among them); and the working rule became 'take main's page and let the checker give the numbers', which is a workaround for a missing generator. THE FIX SHAPE: have the checker PRINT the two numbers and have the page QUOTE a single generated line, so no docs PR edits a number at all - the checker already computes both (it prints 'N documents' and 'B bytes' and compares them against the page), so this is a generator plus one quoted line, not a new measurement. NOT DONE YET - registered here so it is not lost - and the same reasoning is in #310's commit message: 'it stays a conflict magnet until the count is generated rather than typed'. UNTIL THEN: a docs PR takes docs/README.md from main and lets the checker give the numbers, and a re-sync is worth one push only when a merge is REFUSED. THE FIX IS IN #329 (tools/gen_docs_map.py), AND ONE THING THERE IS NOT OBVIOUS: THE PAGE IS INSIDE THE TREE IT MEASURES, SO THE GENERATOR MUST ITERATE TO A FIXED POINT - a one-pass version writes a figure that is already wrong, because writing it changed the page. That was found by running --check on the generator's own output rather than by reading it, and it is the clause that saves the next person the same hour. CLOSED 2026-10-12: the fix is in main. tools/gen_docs_map.py writes the count and the size in all five spots the checker reads, iterating to a fixed point because the page is inside the tree it measures; check_docs_map.py is unchanged and still fails a stale page, and backend/test_docs_map_generator.py covers the loop with a control that bites (one pass is not the fixed point). docs/README.md is now written by the tool, not typed.

REAL DEFECT, FOUND 2026-10-14 WHILE ADDING A DROP-IN FOLDER THAT REPLACES NO PATCH, AND FIXED HERE. scripts/list-plugins.ps1:41 read `$core = @($data.entries | Where-Object { $_.bucket -ne 'plug-in' })`. -Core is declared [switch] in that script's param block, and PowerShell keeps a parameter variable's type, so the assignment failed on EVERY run of the script with: Cannot convert value "System.Object[]" to type "System.Management.Automation.SwitchParameter". REPRODUCED, not reasoned: the HEAD copy of the file (git show HEAD:scripts/list-plugins.ps1, run from scripts\ so RepoRoot is the repository) fails identically in both shells - pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1; and a four-line stand-in of just param([switch]$Core) plus $core = @(...) fails the same way, so the assignment is the cause, not the registry, the backend path or any input. NOTHING CAUGHT IT: the powershell-5 CI job PARSES every .ps1 (a parser error or non-ASCII outside a comment) and never RUNS this one, and no backend suite imports a PowerShell script, so the script was dead on main with every check green. THE FIX: the data variable is $coreRows (used at the count line and in the -Core loop); the -Core switch is untouched. VERIFIED in Windows PowerShell 5.1 against a stand-in backend: list-plugins.ps1 prints the table and "25 drop-in modules, 119 core patches." (24 catalogue folders plus the patch-less one), -Core prints the core table too, and a CI-shaped parse (ParseInput plus the non-ASCII token scan) reports 0 problems for the three scripts this branch touches. HOW IT SURFACED: the receipts feature's folder is not in plugins/registry.json - the catalogue is generated from the patch stack - so add-plugin.ps1 and list-plugins.ps1 had to learn to read such a folder, and there was no way to verify that against a script that could not run at all.
